title: Contraband
text: After the Three Heroes Church incident, whenever I visited the Four Saints Church, they’d sometimes show me things simply because I was a Hero. This was almost exactly the same sort of thing. Why on earth had they been transporting something like this with such reverent care? Come to think of it, didn’t the Three Heroes Church conspire with Trash to outmaneuver the other nations and summon us ahead of schedule?

…Could it be that they stole this from the Four Saints Church and were transporting it from the Three Heroes Church branch in Faubrey to Melromarc!? And what’s more, they must have exploited the Crimson Swine’s brute-forcing of various national borders, including Faubrey’s—no, they must have conspired with the Crimson Swine to smuggle it through. What a prime example of foolishness, I say!

So they’d been hauling around something shady after all. In other words, this very item could be called the reason the Hero Summoning ritual was performed in Melromarc in the first place. …The tool used to summon Father is now in my hands—no, I should hide this somewhere no one will ever find it. That way, the Hero Summoning won’t be able to happen. I’ve already decided as much. And so, I succeeded in eliminating the Crimson Swine, and on top of that, I managed to seize the ritual implement the Three Heroes Church had stolen!
“HAHAHA! A resounding success, I say! Now then, shall we move on to the next order of business!”

There would be no return for the Crimson Swine. Which meant the odds of Big Sister’s village launching its ship before the wave occurred had just dropped! And so I left that place behind. The Crimson Swine and its knights would go missing somewhere in the mountains along the road to Melromarc—now it was just a question of how much time that would buy me.
Now then, what should I do with the days I had left? Time to reorganize the situation once more and go over my checklist.
・Disposal of the Crimson Swine ○ — This went more smoothly than expected, though it still ate up about a day and a half. Three and a half days remain, I say.
・Disposal of Takt and his lot

This is something that will need doing eventually. I’ll also need to investigate what kind of situation Takt’s side is in and how many cards he’s holding… but that’s not exactly top priority right now. Worst case, I could let him swim a while, let him gather up more weapons, then sweep them all up at once—though it does seem a shame not to make use of this current situation.

That said, I can’t afford to get so caught up over there that I neglect something I need to protect. Ah, the fact that I’m looping yet still find it so difficult to apply what I’ve learned to the next attempt is rather trying. I want to do my absolute best, insofar as that’s possible. I need to look into Wolf, and in thinking of some means to determine things, I recalled something. There’s a good chance I can find out whether Claw Hero is still alive just by visiting the scene of Takt’s crime. That area was unnaturally cleared out, with trees snapped, so I should be able to judge whether I’m still in time. Since it’s just a matter of confirming, half a day ought to be enough to check the spot.

It would be best if I could prevent it, but going by the testimony, it’s likely already happened. Still, that’s no excuse to put it off. Confirmation matters, I say. If I take Drive Mode from the nearest portal point and run straight to the crime scene, I should manage just fine.
“Don’t let anyone see you running like that, you hear?”

Father’s voice—the one I failed to save—surfaces in my mind, but that’s surely just my imagination. It’s the fault of that troublesome spear spirit for dragging me into this maddening loop in the first place. Still, thinking about the Hero Summoning, there are a few points that strike me as a bit odd. The way we four were summoned to Melromarc seemed almost like it slipped past some obstruction from the Crimson Swine’s true body. They say the fact that all four of us were summoned reflects the gravity of the situation… but apparently, with reincarnators like Takt scattered all over the place, it seems Heroes have a hard time surviving for long these days. If I were the Crimson Swine’s true body, would I really let the Crimson Swine pull a stunt like this?

Even as I think that, based on past conversations with Father and the spear spirit, I can infer that the true body probably isn’t remotely piloting the Crimson Swine directly. It’s more likely just following some vague subconscious directive—something like “try to make use of the Heroes” at most, I’d wager. To begin with, it may not have been foreseeing the future with certainty that the Hero Summoning would definitely occur in Melromarc. Ark and Hou-kun have both said that foresight in this matter is quite murky at best. Forcibly shaping a convenient future and all that.

That must be difficult in this world. And at the same time, it makes me wonder—there weren’t as many reincarnators like Takt in Melromarc as one might expect, were there? As for why there aren’t many in Melromarc… perhaps the environment of this nation simply isn’t very accommodating to reincarnators. Back when I was a fool, the pigs of this country welcomed me readily enough, since I was nominally a Hero, but the noble pigs of this land have remarkably high pride—ranking above men in status—and apparently there’s a prevailing custom here that men are meant to serve pigs as a matter of course.

Now then, I recall hearing in various progress reports that reincarnators tend to display a rather self-congratulatory streak. That unsettling story about killing a Demi-Human resident of a neighboring village and serving them up as meat is a prime example. Suppose a bunch like that decided to lend a hand because some pig was in trouble. A pig, naturally, takes being helped as a given. Which means no gratitude follows. And when that happens, what does a self-congratulatory reincarnator do?
“What do you mean you’re not grateful to me!” — It’s painfully easy to imagine them snapping like that.

And so the pig, in turn, schemes to get rid of such an insufferable presence. The end result: the reincarnator gets driven out of Melromarc. I do rather wish the ungrateful pig would get a taste of trouble somewhere along the way too. Of course, not every pig is like that—there are some who know their place, pigs who aren’t nobility, so this doesn’t apply across the board. There seem to be other reincarnators scattered about as well… though now that I think of it, back when I was a fool, I did once capture and haul in someone who seemed like a reincarnator myself. And in the previous loop, when Itsuki became Riska, it seems he ran into a few here and there in Melromarc too. That’s the thing—it’s significant that, aside from Trash, no one else in Melromarc possessed a Seven Star Weapon.
So, what should I do next?

・Filolial-sama — What comes to mind is… I’d like to go secure Filolial-sama and the others. Honestly, all this thinking has started to wear thin on me. Ah, I want to see Filolial-sama—no… Filo-tan—as soon as possible…

Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Father Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Father Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Father Father Father Father Father Father Filo-tan Father Father Father Father Father Father Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Father Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan Filo-tan!
“Pick one, it’s creepy!”
“Are you all right, Motoyasu-kun? You seem a bit scrambled.”

For some reason I feel like I can hear Father’s voice, but that’s just how much I miss him, I say. Given how likely it is that I won’t get to see him, it stings all the more. So, to work through these feelings, I’d like to secure Yuki-chan and the others sooner rather than later. And that reminds me… what should I do about Sakura-chan’s egg—the one that will become Filo-tan? There’s a good chance I won’t get to meet Father again, but that’s no reason to give up from the very start, I say. So, I’ll secure the egg that will become Sakura-chan, but hold off on hatching it for a while yet.
“It’s decided, I say!”

Let’s go secure Yuki-chan and the others! Just as I thought that, something with far higher priority surfaced in my mind. Tied up with Filolial-sama as it is, this is a matter I now realize, upon reflection, poses more of an immediate threat than even disposing of the Crimson Swine. And what might that be?… Hurling Rival into that other world, I say! ☆ Send Rival flying into another world! This is something that must take precedence over absolutely everything else. If everything gets wrapped up nicely, it could swoop in from the sidelines, steal credit for my accomplishments, and even pin some baseless crime on me. What’s more, it’s fully capable of spreading rumors to everyone that every single thing I did—including the assassination of the Crimson Swine—was somehow my own wrongdoing. Come what may, I will not let it have its way in this loop, I say!

“Stop unilaterally branding Gaelion the villain and playing the victim, nano! Nano, nano! The next time Gaelion gets sent over there, Gaelion will make sure to pay you back accordingly, so you’d better be ready, nano!”
Rival said this so many times my ears practically grew calluses from it, but I shall not be ready, I say! You just go and keep that other world peaceful all on your own, I say!
